messages:
maria chen: heads up — during mag-13b-int4v2 bring-up I saw a small but consistent token shift after long priming (~6.5k). phrases start to drift/repeat a token earlier than fp16 baseline :eyes:

maria chen: quick dump shows kv index mismatch around token 5234, not an off-by-one in model code, looks like an aliasing in RoPE mapping after quantized prefill. excerpt from debug:```
KV_CHECK: pos=5234 expected=0x12 got=0x13 ropemap=notch
TRACE: priming_len=6520 batch=1 quant_mode=INT4V2
```

samir patel: yikes. can you repro deterministically with a short harness? put the same long prompt and compare next-token logprobs vs fp16?

maria chen: yes repro script here (local):```python
# run_repro.py
run_model('mag-13b-int4v2', prompt='long_dialogue.txt', max_new_tokens=256, dump_kv=True)
```
works for me 9/10. can share seed and prompt privately.

lee: @maria any config differences? rotary scaling/prefix-clamp? sometimes we apply a small per-layer scale for int4 that causes phase aliasing.

maria chen: checked — used default quant scale profile from onboarder. no manual per-layer tweak. ropemap seems to be using the new "notch" downsample in compiler.

alex r: when you enable strict kv sanity checks we saw latency jump 30-40% under concurrent traffic — that might be why this only surfaces in single-shot long priming vs canary. do you see latency spikes?

maria chen: yes, enabling kv-checker adds ~35ms/token on our mag64 GPU. but mismatch occurs even without checker (we only noticed via downstream text diff).

samir patel: next steps I suggest:
- reproduce with fixed seed and attach full kv digest
- run compare: fp16 vs int4v2 with/without "notch" ropemap
- try a patched ropemap that preserves high-freq phase for >4k positions

lee: I'll try a quick run. also try toggling compile flag `--rotary-interp=linear` vs `notched` to see if aliasing disappears.

ci-bot: CI matrix triggered: quant-priming/regression (mag-13b-int4v2) — nightly-priming-eval queued (run id: 2026-03-21_0421) :robot_face:

ops-jen: FYI if you plan to replicate on Dedicated please limit concurrency — we've seen OOM when the job pairs with dynamic batching >2x on mag64.

maria chen: quick numbers from local runs (single-host, batch=1):
- fp16 baseline: avg token latency 18ms, no drift over 10k tokens
- int4v2 notched: avg token latency 21ms, drift at ~6.5k
- int4v2 linear: avg token latency 20ms, drift reduced but still present at >8k

alex r: interesting. seems like interpolation changes the drift point. could be RoPE precision loss + kv alignment. can you capture kv fingerprints (small hash per pos) and diff position-wise?

maria chen: attaching short CSV (pseudodump) — pos, kv_hash_fp16, kv_hash_int4v2. differences start around 5200, cluster every ~128 tokens.

samir patel: cluster every 128 tokens -> smells like a quant stride/tiling artifact. maybe our kernel tiling copies in 128-chunk windows and rounding accumulates.

lee: I'll instrument kernel to avoid fractional remainder copy and run nfuzz across tile sizes (64/128/256). will post results in thread.

maria chen: low-priority workaround for canary: pin canary traffic to fp16 for prompts >6k until we have root cause. not ideal but safe.

ops-jen: created a short incident ticket INC-2026-0421, assigned to @samir and @lee. Temporary route/flag added to routing rules: if priming_len > 6000 && model_tag == 'int4v2-notched' -> route to fallback fp16.

ci-bot: test update: nightly run started (will post artifact link once finished).

samir patel: I'll start a bisect between compiler commits that introduced notched ropemap. also try a quick quantization rebuild with updated scale heuristics.

lee: nfuzz results: tile=64/256 look clean, tile=128 reproduces drift with same cluster spacing. pushing patch that pads tiles to avoid fractional int4 vector tail. will create PR.

maria chen: awesome. once PR lands I'll re-run onboarder and smoke canary. thanks 🙏 :party_parrot:

alex r: keep an eye on latency after padding — if padding increases memory bandwidth we might need to tweak batch autoscale.

maria chen: noted. will coordinate with infra for a small canary (5% traffic) after fix validated.

ops-jen: leaving note: hold Dedicated upgrades touching mag64 kernel until this is resolved.

ci-bot: artifact: s3://redwood-ci/quant-priming/1758004321/artifacts.tar.gz (uploaded)

maria chen: uploaded repro + diffs to the ticket. I'll follow up with a short eval comparing perplexity + token-match rate across priming lengths (4k/6k/8k) once PR merges.

samir patel: plan sounds good. if patch reduces cluster diffs to <0.01% at 8k we can roll int4v2 back into canary. otherwise fallback to fp16 for long prompts.

lee: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infer/pull/8421 — includes padded tiling + unit test.

maria chen: thx all — will monitor results and post final regression table here.
